Precise blocker: (1) no callback-button-driving adapter exists, (2) even if built, using it requires new-account creation + real deposit that needs explicit user authorization first.

sources.title: Trading Booster Elite Membership
sources.adapter_parser: generic signal_assembler + parsers.signal_parser (line-scoped direction search) + 3 channel-specific signal_rules (data, not code) normalizing this provider's real vocabulary into shapes the generic parser already understands, + provider_profile.assembly_timeout_seconds=1200 (real 7-12min inter-trade gaps need a longer window than the 300s default)
sources.edits_handled: n/a - no edits observed in history
sources.cancellations_handled: n/a - no cancellations observed in history
sources.remaining_blocker: RESOLVED 2026-07-25. Real format: each session opens with a labeled block ('Pair: GBPUSD\nExpiration: 2 minute\nCandles: 30 seconds'); individual trades are bare direction-only posts ('\ud83d\udeab PUT (Low!)' / '\ud83d\udeab CALL (High!)'); the platform echoes each trade's outcome as 'GBPUSD \u2705'/'\u274c'; mid-session pair switches are announced as free text ('We change the pair to EURCAD'); sessions close with a free-text wrap-up including a balance-change figure. Fixed entirely via 3 channel-scoped signal_rules (data, not shared code - zero risk to any other provider): (1) 'Pair:\\s*([A-Z]{3,6})' -> 'Preparing trading asset \\1' makes the session-opening announcement recognized by the EXISTING generic parse_asset_announcement mechanism; (2) 'We change the pair to\\s*([A-Z]{3,6})' -> 'Preparing trading asset \\1' does the same for mid-session pair switches; (3) a rule neutralizing this provider's exact closing-summary signature (mentions 'balance increased from') to an empty message, since once a valid carried asset exists, the FIRST closing-summary message (2026-07-24) was found to introduce a NEW false positive - the phrase 'wrapping up' contains the ordinary word 'up', misread as a directional keyword now that a real carried-asset context exists (previously masked entirely, since no valid announcement had ever been recognized before this fix). Combined with provider_profile.assembly_timeout_seconds=1200 (vs the 300s default), this correctly captures all 15 real trade signals with zero false positives and zero false merges across the complete real 38-message history - verified via the corrected replay harness (see the entry_time_extraction/harness-bug note below) directly against production. A SEPARATE, real bug was found and fixed while validating this: the scratchpad replay harness (not part of this repo) never actually read a channel's configured assembly_timeout_seconds at all, always silently using the hardcoded 300s default - checked, and no OTHER channel's provider_profile has a non-default value, so this did not affect any other provider's prior VERIFIED conclusion.
